timeline.description: Scenes and events in the order they happen in the story, which is not always the order you tell them in.

order.label: Narrative order
order.description: Shows where each scene sits in the manuscript and marks the ones that go back in time.

checks.overlap: {names} is also somewhere else at the same time: “{title}”. | {names} are also somewhere else at the same time: “{title}”.
checks.count: {n} overlap to check | {n} overlaps to check

undated.title: Undated
undated.nothing: Scenes and events without a date wait here.
undated.hint: They are not on the timeline yet: a date, even just the year, is enough.
undated.noneFiltered: With these filters, nothing is left undated.

errors.dayRange: This day does not exist in the chosen month.

when.label: Date as written in the story
when.labelHelp: Shown instead of the date: useful for invented calendars.
when.labelPlaceholder: For example: Third moon of the year 312

event.panelDescription: Something that happens in the story, or in history, with its date and who is part of it.
event.missing: This event is gone: it may be in the trash.
event.title: Title of the event
event.descriptionPlaceholder: Tell the event: what happens and why it matters to the story.

empty.title: The timeline puts scenes and events in order: give a scene a date and you will see it here.
empty.guide: A date can be a year, a month, a day or an exact moment: “1953” and “14 November 1953, 22:10” fall into line by themselves. For an invented calendar, also write the date as it appears in the story.
empty.dateFirst: Give the first scene a date
empty.filtered: No scene or event matches the filters.

entity.emptyHint: An event is something that happens before the scenes or outside them: a birth, a war, a meeting. It also appears on the timeline.
